subject: Private connectivity options — network access patterns, allowlist CSV, and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bowen <laura.bowen@nebulaanalytics.com>
Cc: Chris Park <chris.park@nebulaanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private connectivity options — network access patterns, allowlist CSV, and next steps

Hi Laura / Chris,

Thanks again for taking time today — good conversation. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the deployment options we discussed (hosted API, dedicated capacity, private VPC/on-prem) and call out the specific networking pieces we need to validate to move a Private VPC forward.

Quick recap and asks:
- Preferred deployment: you indicated a preference for Private VPC with PrivateLink to keep traffic inside your AWS account, but still evaluating peering for dev/test.
- Networking items we need from your side:
  1) Egress model: confirm whether outbound connections from the Redwood runtime should use your NAT gateways or Redwood-managed egress (this affects IP allowlist strategy).
  2) PrivateLink vs Peering: if PrivateLink, we need the service consumer VPC ID(s) and account IDs for the interface endpoints; if peering, we need the VPC CIDR ranges and route table owners.
  3) Allowlist CSV: we've attached an IP allowlist template to populate with the subnets/egress IPs you expect to use for app traffic and any preferred secondary ranges.
  4) TLS termination & certs: confirm whether you will provide certs or prefer Redwood to terminate at the interface.

What I'll do next:
- Attach our network checklist and a short deployment matrix with timelines (attached).
- Once you populate the allowlist CSV, we can scope the Dedicated vs Private pricing delta and provide a one-week target for a staging Private VPC preview.

Please let me know if I missed anything — otherwise, can you fill the attached ip-allowlist-template.csv and return by EOD Thursday (28 Aug)? That will keep us on the one-week staging window.

Thanks,

Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
[Attachment: net-connect-checklist.pdf (PDF, 58 KB)]
[Attachment: ip-allowlist-template.csv (CSV, 2 KB)]
[Attachment: redwood-deploy-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 23 KB)]

From: Laura Bowen <laura.bowen@nebulaanalytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Park <chris.park@nebulaanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:41:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity options — network access patterns, allowlist CSV, and next steps

Thanks Olga — helpful summary. A few clarifying notes from our side:

1) Egress: For prod we must use our own NAT gateways (security requirement). For dev/test we are open to Redwood-managed egress to simplify the preview.
2) PrivateLink: preferred for prod due to stricter control, but we may do VPC peering for the dev sandbox.
3) IP allowlist template: attaching our populated CSV (see attached) — added our primary NAT egress IPs and a /28 we use for service-to-service traffic.
4) Certs: we will bring certs to terminate at our ALB in front of the consumer endpoint (so Redwood will not terminate TLS).

Two questions: (a) What minimum throughput SLAs should we expect for a 4-GPU dedicated staging (roughly 3000 qps peak)? (b) If we start with a PrivateLink preview, can we flip traffic to a peered model later without redeploying the model?

I'll get the CSV back to you by EOD Thursday as requested (we already have an internal copy attached).

Best,
Laura
VP Product, Nebula Analytics
laura.bowen@nebulaanalytics.com
[Attachment: nebula_ip_allowlist_populated.csv (CSV, 3 KB)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bowen <laura.bowen@nebulaanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity options — network access patterns, allowlist CSV, and next steps

Laura — perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround and for populating the CSV. Couple of answers inline:

- SLA / throughput: for a 4-GPU Dedicated pool in our Dedicated tier we typically neutralize to an operational target of 95th percentile tail latency under 200 ms for small completions and sustained throughput consistent with ~2.5–3k qps depending on model family. We'll confirm exact numbers for the model you'll pin, but that's the ballpark; Ben will follow up with a short benchmark summary.
- PrivateLink -> Peering migration: yes — the runtime and model pinning are independent of the connectivity layer. We can route at the load balancer/route table level, so switching from PrivateLink to peering is a networking cutover; no model redeploy required. We'll validate compatibility with your security team during the staging window.

Next steps:
1) Ben to share the benchmark snapshot and proposed Dedicated capacity numbers.
2) Marissa (customer engineering) will schedule a 60-minute network runbook call with your infra team — suggested slots next Tue/Wed.
3) We'll provision a short-lived staging PrivateLink endpoint after we confirm your VPC IDs and the completed allowlist. Expect that to take 3–4 business days once we have the final CSV and account IDs.

Looping Ben & Marissa into this thread — Ben, can you add the bench numbers and a short note on cost delta between Dedicated and Private? Marissa, please propose two times for the infra runbook.

Thanks,
Olga

[Quoted text hidden]
[Attachment forwarded: nebula_ip_allowlist_populated.csv]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bowen <laura.bowen@nebulaanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity options — network access patterns, allowlist CSV, and next steps

Hi all — quick follow-up with the numbers Olga promised. Attached is a short benchmark snapshot (model: redwood-base-13b, quantized) run on a 4xA10 pool we use as a proxy for Dedicated staging. Highlights:
- Median token latency: 85 ms
- 95th percentile token latency: 180 ms under steady-state batching
- Approx cost delta: Private VPC + Dedicated pool is ~1.6x hosted API unit cost in our estimates for your 3k qps outline (includes dedicated infra premium + private connectivity overhead).

For the runbook call, Marissa proposed: Tue Sep 1 10:00 AM PT or Wed Sep 2 2:00 PM PT. Laura — please confirm which works best for infra and security.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123
[Attachment: redwood-benchmark-4GPU.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]
